name: bitsandbytes NF4 (4-bit NormalFloat)
notes: NF4 is a data type, not a PTQ algorithm: 16 fixed quantization points chosen to be information-theoretically optimal for normally-distributed weights, with a per-block absmax scale and optional double quantization of those scales (quant-torch-qlora-paper). Bitsandbytes' HF docs position it as memory reduction for loading, with LLM.int8() as the accuracy-preserving compute path - i.e. NF4 quantization for storage, 8-bit compute for the outliers. Weight-only, so again no native 4-bit activation path. Block size 64 is the bitsandbytes default and is a library default rather than something NF4 the format defines; recorded as such. It became the default quantization for QLoRA finetuning (quant-torch-qlora-paper), which is why it is ubiquitous - its inference story is weaker than AWQ/GPTQ. No fp16 quality delta recorded: the source paper is a finetuning paper and does not report a clean NF4-vs-fp16 inference benchmark delta.
